name: Funds, Co-Investments and Manager Selection
summary: LP diligence on a GP raising a commingled fund (buyout, venture, credit, real estate, hedge), a co-investment alongside a GP, or a fund-of-funds, OCIO or SMA program. The LP cannot fire the manager, litigation is not a remedy, and since the SEC Private Fund Adviser rules were vacated (June 5, 2024) no federal rule requires quarterly statements, fund audits or GP-led fairness opinions, so every protection must be in the LPA or side letter. The spine is: ILPA DDQ 2.0 baseline; full operational due diligence with unsolicited service-provider calls scored against the Trust and Delegation base rates and the 12 SEC exam-deficiency test steps; fee economics against Metrick-Yasuda and fee-tier evidence with MFN to the best tier; track record rebuilt from cash flows with PME, with and without the sub line, NAV-loan distributions and top exits, against survivor-inclusive, factor-appropriate benchmarks; deal-level attribution and carry split by person; co-invest adverse-selection tests; allocator governance and pacing.
one_check: Call the administrator, the auditor, the custodian and the named valuation firm yourself, unsolicited, and reconcile what each says to what the GP told you; for allocators, compare the fund size, team and strategy you are buying with those that produced the track record rebuilt from cash flows against a survivor-inclusive, factor-appropriate benchmark.

subtypes.name: Buyout fund
subtypes.description: Closed-end leveraged buyout fund; benchmark against PME and a levered small-value index.

subtypes.name: Venture fund
subtypes.description: Closed-end VC fund; right-tail returns, test with and without top outcomes; partner-level attribution.

subtypes.name: Credit fund
subtypes.description: Private credit, direct lending, CLO or opportunistic credit fund; put-writing benchmark; insurer-affiliated managers.

subtypes.name: Real estate fund
subtypes.description: Closed-end real estate fund; levered public-REIT benchmark; related-party property fees.

subtypes.name: Hedge fund
subtypes.description: Liquid or semi-liquid hedge fund; monthly returns, MPPM, put-writing benchmark, prime-broker confirmation.

subtypes.name: Co-investment
subtypes.description: Direct stake alongside a GP's fund in a single deal via SPV or direct holding; adverse-selection tests plus full company diligence.

subtypes.name: Fund-of-funds / SMA / OCIO / allocator
subtypes.description: Second-layer vehicle or allocator program; pacing, roster, delegation, fees on active assets.

intake_questions.question: Is this a commitment to a buyout, venture, credit, real estate or hedge fund, a co-investment alongside a GP, or a fund-of-funds, SMA or OCIO mandate?
intake_questions.why: Selects the subtype and which request items apply.

intake_questions.question: Is this the manager's first fund, or a successor fund? If successor, how large is it relative to the funds that earned the track record?
intake_questions.why: Emerging managers need heavier ODD and prior-firm attribution; size growth weakens persistence.

intake_questions.question: Does the fund use, or may it use, a subscription line, NAV facility or other fund-level leverage?
intake_questions.why: Triggers with/without-facility performance and Chapter 14 terms.

intake_questions.question: Has the manager sponsored any GP-led secondary or continuation vehicle?
intake_questions.why: Triggers GP-led history and Chapter 13 protections.

intake_questions.question: Is the manager affiliated with an insurer whose general account provides permanent capital?
intake_questions.why: Triggers statutory-statement, RBC and affiliated-placement checks.

intake_questions.question: For a co-investment: is the co-invest alongside a family office or club, and is the main fund taking its full pro rata?
intake_questions.why: Triggers Archegos aggregate-exposure check and adverse-selection tests.

intake_questions.question: What commitment size are we offering, and where does it sit against the fee-tier thresholds?
intake_questions.why: Determines achievable tier and MFN negotiation.

intake_questions.question: Does the strategy use options, leverage or short-volatility exposures (credit, merger arb, market neutral)?
Does the portfolio include healthcare or government-contract companies?
intake_questions.why: Triggers secondary-liability (FCA, ERISA) review and Chapter 17.

intake_questions.question: Is this a thematic vehicle (AI, crypto, space, climate)?
Are we diligencing an allocator, fund-of-funds or OCIO rather than a single GP?
intake_questions.why: Triggers the 12.2 B allocator document set.

requests.request: Private placement memorandum, draft LPA, subscription documents and side-letter template for the fund being offered.
requests.format: Current drafts as circulated to all LPs, with version date; redline against the predecessor fund's executed LPA.
requests.why: Governance is contractual only: the LP cannot fire the manager, so the documents are the only protection.
requests.pass: All four documents received; LPA contains a key-person clause, a for-cause removal right and an audit covenant (tested in later items).
requests.fail: Documents withheld until after a soft commitment, or LPA lacks key-person and removal provisions entirely.
requests.verify: Compare against the predecessor fund's executed LPA obtained from an existing LP or the administrator.

requests.request: Completed ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0, all 20 sections (Firm, Fund, Succession and Key Persons, Investment Strategy, Co-Investments, GP-Led Secondaries, Credit Facilities, Investment Process, Team, Alignment of Interests, Market Environment, Fund Terms, Firm Governance/Risk/Compliance, Track Record, Accounting and Valuation, Reporting, Legal, Data Security and Technology, ESG, DEI).
requests.format: ILPA DDQ 2.0 (2021) format, signed by the CCO or COO, dated within 90 days.
requests.why: The standard baseline; answers are diffed against the data room to catch misstatements (42% of managers have at least one misrepresentation or inconsistency).
requests.pass: Every section answered; zero answers contradicted by data-room documents; refused or deflected questions logged and resolved.
requests.fail: Sections left blank, 'available on request' answers, or any answer contradicted by a primary document.
requests.verify: Diff every factual DDQ answer against the data room, Form ADV and service-provider confirmations; log each refusal (count and topic) in the A.2 report.

requests.request: ILPA DDQ 2.0 Appendix A requested-document set (stated as 89 documents by an aggregator).
requests.format: Index mapping each Appendix A document to a data-room file, with any omissions explained.
requests.why: Missing standard documents are where a first-time manager's story falls apart.
requests.pass: Every Appendix A document provided or a written reason given for each omission; confirm the count against the ILPA document itself.
requests.fail: More than a handful of Appendix A documents missing without reason.
requests.verify: Check the count and list against the ILPA DDQ 2.0 publication, not the aggregator.

requests.request: List of every fund, vehicle, SMA, co-invest vehicle and side vehicle the firm and its principals have ever managed, including closed, abandoned and wound-down vehicles.
requests.format: Schedule with vehicle name, vintage, size, strategy, status, auditor and administrator for each; signed by the CFO.
requests.why: Survivorship: managers drop dead or abandoned vehicles from the track record.
requests.pass: List is complete against Form ADV Schedule D private-fund listings, prior PPMs and service-provider confirmations; every vehicle appears in the performance schedule.
requests.fail: Any vehicle found in ADV, press, litigation or prior PPMs that is missing from the list.
requests.verify: Reconcile to Form ADV Section 7.B.1 listings over all available years and ask the administrator and auditor to list every vehicle they service for the manager.

requests.request: ILPA Performance Template for each prior fund: gross and net IRR and TVPI, each with and without the fund-level subscription facility (granular or gross-up method), with sub-line interest as a separate expense line.
requests.format: ILPA Performance Template (published 2025), one per fund, prepared or tied out by the administrator.
requests.why: Subscription lines inflate IRR with no change in multiple; refusal to show with/without figures is a signal.
requests.pass: Template delivered for every prior fund; with- and without-facility figures both shown; ties to fund cash flows within rounding.
requests.fail: Refusal, figures only 'with facility', or template not reconcilable to cash flows.
requests.verify: Recompute IRR without the facility from dated LP capital calls supplied by the administrator.

requests.request: Quarterly ILPA Reporting Template history for every prior fund still reporting (2016 template, or the updated template for funds in their investment period in Q1 2026 or launched on or after Jan. 1, 2026).
requests.format: Quarterly ILPA Reporting Templates as sent to LPs, complete since each fund's first close.
requests.why: Shows fees, expenses, offsets and facility usage as actually reported to LPs over time.
requests.pass: Unbroken quarterly series; fees and offsets reconcile to audited financials.
requests.fail: Gaps in the series, non-ILPA bespoke reporting only, or fees that do not tie to audits.
requests.verify: Obtain the same quarterly reports from an existing LP reference and compare.

requests.request: Dated fund-level cash flows (every capital call, distribution and NAV) for every prior fund and vehicle.
requests.format: Administrator-produced ledger in electronic form, one row per cash flow, with quarterly NAVs.
requests.why: Needed to rebuild IRR, TVPI, DPI, PME, KS-PME and GPME independently of the manager's marketing figures.
requests.pass: Ledger covers all vehicles on the vehicle list; rebuilt IRR, TVPI and DPI match reported figures within rounding.
requests.fail: Cash flows unavailable, sponsor-produced only, or rebuilt figures differ from marketing figures.
requests.verify: Request the ledger directly from the administrator and rebuild performance ourselves.

requests.request: Form ADV Parts 1 and 2 for every adviser entity, with a reconciliation of each Item 11 disciplinary disclosure to the DDQ answers.
requests.format: Current filing plus all prior amendments for 5 years; reconciliation table prepared by the CCO.
requests.why: 41% of managers have a past legal or regulatory problem and 21% misrepresented it; ADV history predicts operational risk.
requests.pass: Every ADV disclosure matches the DDQ; no undisclosed legal, regulatory or disciplinary item.
requests.fail: Any ADV item missing from or contradicted by the DDQ; adviser not registered and no reason given.
requests.verify: Pull ADV directly from IAPD; do not use the manager's copy. Where no ADV exists, estimate an omega score from public performance, volatility, size, age and fees.

requests.request: All SEC examination correspondence, deficiency letters, Wells notices and the manager's responses for the last 5 years.
requests.format: Complete letters and responses, not summaries; CCO certification that the set is complete.
requests.why: SEC deficiency findings map directly to the fee, valuation and conflict failures LPs suffer.
requests.pass: Full set produced; every deficiency shown as remediated with evidence; no open Wells notice.
requests.fail: Refusal, summary only, open Wells notice, or repeat deficiencies across exams.
requests.verify: Ask in the DDQ, in the meeting and in the side letter rep; compare with SEC enforcement releases and press.

requests.request: Service-provider list with named contacts: administrator, custodian, prime broker(s), auditor, valuation agent, legal counsel, bank(s).
requests.format: Firm names, engagement start dates, named relationship contacts with independently verifiable switchboard numbers.
requests.why: Enables the unsolicited calls that catch Madoff, Infinity Q and SQN.
requests.pass: Each function is held by a separate, independent firm; contacts given; consent to direct contact provided in writing.
requests.fail: Any function performed in-house or by an affiliate; refusal of consent to direct contact.
requests.verify: Look up each provider's switchboard independently (not from the manager's list) before calling.

requests.request: Structure chart of the fund complex showing which firm acts as manager, administrator, custodian, broker-dealer/prime broker and auditor.
requests.format: Legal-entity chart with ownership percentages and service agreements listed for each box.
requests.why: The Madoff structure had one firm acting as manager, broker-dealer, custodian and administrator.
requests.pass: Manager, administrator, custodian, prime broker and auditor are separate unaffiliated firms; administrator computes NAV from its own records.
requests.fail: Self-administration, affiliated custodian or broker, or administrator relying on manager-supplied records.
requests.verify: Confirm independence of each provider by checking ownership in their own filings and on the direct calls.

requests.request: Confirmation that every fund and vehicle managed has been audited every year, with auditor name and opinion type by year.
requests.format: Schedule of audits by vehicle and year, with copies of each audit opinion page.
requests.why: An unaudited fund is an automatic pass (Momentum Advisors).
requests.pass: Every vehicle audited annually with an unqualified opinion.
requests.fail: Any unaudited vehicle; qualified opinions; late statements.
requests.verify: Call the auditor to confirm each engagement and opinion.

requests.request: Organization chart, biographies of all investment professionals, and every departure in the last 5 years with reason.
requests.format: Current org chart; departures list with name, title, date, reason and where they went.
requests.why: Track records borrowed from people who left; senior departures predict fundraising trouble.
requests.pass: Departures list complete against LinkedIn, ADV and prior PPMs; no unexplained senior departures.
requests.fail: Undisclosed departures found independently; senior departures clustered before this fundraise.
requests.verify: Cross-check departures against prior PPMs and call two former senior employees.

requests.request: Fund-size, team-size and deal-count history: each fund's size, number of senior investment professionals, deals per year and deals per partner.
requests.format: Table by fund vintage; AUM growth by year.
requests.why: Size is the enemy of performance; doubling deal pace without doubling the operating bench is a yellow flag.
requests.pass: Successor fund size growth matched by senior-team growth; deals per partner not rising sharply.
requests.fail: Successor fund much larger than the funds that earned the track record, or deal pace or AUM doubling without the bench doubling.
requests.verify: Verify team counts against ADV employee counts and the org chart history.

requests.request: Stated target net return, the benchmark the manager claims to beat, and a table of prior funds' projected versus actual net returns.
requests.format: Manager's written statement plus original PPM projections for each prior fund.
requests.why: Alpha in alternatives is hard to verify; projections above the outside view need specific evidence.
requests.pass: Target net return stated against a named, factor-appropriate benchmark; prior projections within reasonable range of outcomes.
requests.fail: Generic buyout strategy projecting 20%+ net IRR with no specific evidence; prior projections systematically missed.
requests.verify: Compare original PPM projections (from existing LPs) with realized outcomes.

requests.request: Required annual deployment for this fund against the size of the strategy's addressable market.
requests.format: Deployment plan by year and market-size source.
requests.why: Very large deployment targets make selective underwriting hard (largest perpetual private-credit fund must deploy about $43B a year, over a quarter of US direct lending).
requests.pass: Annual deployment is a small share of the addressable market with a sourced market estimate.
requests.fail: Deployment requirement is a material share of the market or no market sizing exists.
requests.verify: Check market size against independent sources in the bible's Chapter 4 and 15 references.

requests.request: Litigation list for the firm and each principal, including arbitrations and settled matters.
requests.format: Schedule with court, case number, parties, status and outcome.
requests.why: 32% of managers were defendants in legal disputes; 10% would pass a DDQ and are caught only by an independent check.
requests.pass: Complete against independent court searches run by the universal background check; no undisclosed matters.
requests.fail: Any matter found independently that is not on the list.
requests.verify: Reconcile to the universal background-check report and docket searches.

requests.request: Full fee-tier schedule for this fund: management-fee and carry rates for every tier, and the commitment thresholds and other criteria for each tier.
requests.format: Schedule signed by the GP; MFN compendium showing which tiers exist.
requests.why: Within a fund, tiers differ by about 91 bp of management fee and 5.8 points of carry on average; a 90 bp gap compounds over 10 years.
requests.pass: Full schedule disclosed; our net terms equal the best tier or the difference is explained by a documented threshold we do not meet.
requests.fail: Tiers not disclosed, or the MFN excludes the best tier.
requests.verify: Compare with fee terms reported by other LPs and the MFN compendium.

requests.request: All side letters granted in this fund (or the MFN compendium), with a list of liquidity, information, fee and co-invest rights granted to any investor.
requests.format: Redacted side letters or full MFN compendium; GP certification of completeness.
requests.why: Preferential liquidity or information terms are a recurring SEC exam deficiency.
requests.pass: Every liquidity and information right granted to another LP is either offered to us or justified; no undisclosed preferential terms.
requests.fail: Side-letter terms withheld; preferential liquidity granted to some investors only.
requests.verify: Compare with MFN elections circulated after final close; ask fund counsel to confirm.

requests.request: Management-fee terms: rate, fee basis during and after the investment period, step-down or switch to invested capital, and treatment of sold, written-down and written-off investments.
requests.format: LPA fee section and a worked example of the fee base after the investment period.
requests.why: Fee base not stepped down after write-downs is a recurring SEC finding; fixed fees are 60% to two-thirds of GP revenue.
requests.pass: Fee basis switches to net invested capital after the investment period and steps down for realizations and write-downs (buyout market practice 84%; VC 43%).
requests.fail: Fee stays on committed capital for the full term, or no reduction for write-downs.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review against ILPA Principles 3.0 and Metrick and Yasuda benchmarks.

requests.request: Carried-interest terms: carry rate, basis (committed or invested), hurdle rate, catch-up percentage and calculation example.
requests.format: LPA waterfall section with a numeric worked example.
requests.why: Hurdle and carry basis determine how much of GP revenue depends on performance.
requests.pass: Buyout: hurdle present (93.1% of buyout funds), within the 6% to 10% band (8% modal); catch-up disclosed. VC: hurdle often absent (47.6% have one); carry basis disclosed.
requests.fail: No hurdle in a buyout fund without a fee concession; catch-up or basis not disclosed.

requests.request: Waterfall type (whole-fund or deal-by-deal) and the interim clawback mechanics.
requests.why: Deal-by-deal waterfalls pay carry before LPs are made whole.
requests.pass: Whole-fund (European) waterfall, or deal-by-deal with interim clawback testing and escrow.
requests.fail: Deal-by-deal with no escrow and clawback only at fund end.

requests.request: GP clawback provision with personal or entity guarantees from each carry recipient.
requests.format: LPA clawback clause plus executed guarantee forms or guarantee entity financials.
requests.why: A clawback without guarantees is unenforceable against departed partners.
requests.pass: Clawback is net of taxes at most, backed by several (or joint and several) guarantees from carry recipients or a creditworthy entity.
requests.fail: No guarantees, or guarantee from a shell entity with no assets.

requests.request: GP commitment: amount, percentage of fund, source (cash versus management-fee waiver), and how funded by each partner.
requests.format: LPA GP-commitment clause and a schedule by partner.
requests.why: Alignment: GP commitment size and form.
requests.pass: GP commitment funded in cash, disclosed by partner; fee-waiver funding disclosed and limited.
requests.fail: Commitment funded mainly by fee waivers or concentrated in one founder.
requests.verify: Confirm with the administrator that the GP commitment was funded in prior funds on the same terms as LPs.

requests.request: Portfolio-company fee offset provision: treatment of transaction, monitoring, director, exit and break-up fees.
requests.why: Undisclosed or unshared portfolio-company fees are among the most common SEC findings (TZP; Blackstone).
requests.pass: 100% of portfolio-company fees offset against the management fee (market: about 80% of LPAs share; a third return 100%, a third split 50/50).
requests.fail: Offset below 100% without disclosure; fees to GP affiliates excluded from the offset.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review; recompute in confirmatory.

requests.request: Clause prohibiting acceleration of monitoring fees on exit or IPO.
requests.why: Blackstone advisers accelerated monitoring fees on exits without adequate disclosure ($12.5M penalty plus $37.5M disgorgement).
requests.pass: Express prohibition on monitoring-fee acceleration, or 100% offset of any accelerated amount.
requests.fail: Silence on acceleration, or acceleration permitted and not offset.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review; check monitoring agreements in confirmatory.

requests.request: Key-person clause: named persons, trigger, investment-period suspension, and dissolution or LP vote mechanics.
requests.why: Exit rights substitute for control; the key-person clause must name the people who actually decide.
requests.pass: Key-person names match the partners who lead deals and sit on the IC; trigger causes automatic suspension with LP vote to dissolve or reinstate.
requests.fail: Key persons are not the deal leads; no suspension; no dissolution right.
requests.verify: Match names to the deal-attribution schedule and IC minutes.

requests.request: For-cause removal provision: cause definition, LP vote threshold, who determines cause, and economics on removal.
requests.why: LPs cannot fire the manager except through this clause; a fund with neither key-person dissolution nor a workable removal right has no governance.
requests.pass: Cause includes fraud, wilful misconduct, material breach and key-person failure; determination does not require a final non-appealable judgment; vote threshold achievable.
requests.fail: Cause requires a final court judgment, or threshold unachievable given LP concentration.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review against ILPA Principles 3.0.

requests.request: No-fault divorce provision: vote threshold to remove the GP or terminate the investment period without cause, and economics on exercise.
requests.why: Contract is the only governance; no-fault divorce is the backstop when cause cannot be proven.
requests.pass: No-fault removal or termination right exists with a stated supermajority threshold.
requests.fail: No no-fault right, combined with a narrow cause definition.

requests.request: LPAC provisions: composition, appointment, and consent rights over affiliated transactions, cross-trades, GP-led secondaries, NAV facilities and term extensions.
requests.format: LPA LPAC section and current LPAC membership.
requests.why: LPAC consent skipped for conflicted transactions is a recurring SEC finding.
requests.pass: LPAC of independent LPs must consent to affiliated transactions, GP-leds, NAV facilities and term extensions.
requests.fail: LPAC consent not required for any of these, or LPAC dominated by GP-affiliated LPs.

requests.request: Subscription-line terms in the LPA: maximum size as % of commitments, maximum days outstanding, and an LP opt-out offered at the outset.
requests.format: LPA borrowing clause and side-letter opt-out mechanics.
requests.why: Sub lines inflate IRR; ILPA Principles 3.0 call for reasonable size and duration and an opt-out.
requests.pass: Cap at or below 15% to 25% of commitments and 180 days outstanding (ILPA PE reference points), with LP opt-out.
requests.fail: No cap, outstanding beyond 180 days permitted without disclosure, or no opt-out.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review against ILPA 2020 guidance and Principles 3.0.

requests.request: NAV-facility provisions: fund-level leverage cap, LPAC consent regardless of use of proceeds, no carry on NAV-loan-funded distributions, disclosure of recallability.
requests.why: NAV-funded distributions inflate IRR and DPI and may be recallable; carry may be paid on borrowed money.
requests.pass: LPAC consent required for any NAV facility; no carry on NAV-funded distributions; recall terms disclosed.
requests.fail: NAV borrowing permitted without consent, or carry payable on borrowed distributions.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review against ILPA NAV guidance (July 2024).

requests.request: GP-led secondary provisions: LPAC consent, true status quo option, fairness opinion from a provider with no other GP mandate, minimum 30-day election period.
requests.why: No federal rule requires a fairness opinion on a GP-led since June 2024.
requests.pass: All four protections present.
requests.fail: Any protection absent.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review against ILPA Continuation Funds guidance (May 2023).

requests.request: Information-rights covenant: quarterly ILPA Reporting Template and annual ILPA Performance Template (with and without the sub line), with delivery deadlines.
requests.format: LPA reporting clause or side letter.
requests.why: Since June 2024 no federal rule requires quarterly fee or performance statements.
requests.pass: Both templates contractually required with deadlines.
requests.fail: Reporting at GP discretion or in a bespoke format only.

requests.request: Audit covenant: annual audit of the fund by a named auditor of adequate size, with a delivery deadline.
requests.format: LPA clause naming the auditor or auditor standard.
requests.why: No federal rule requires a fund audit beyond the Custody Rule audit option.
requests.pass: Annual audit by a named auditor sized for the mandate; delivery deadline stated.
requests.fail: No audit covenant, or auditor unnamed and replaceable without notice.

requests.request: Legal review of the LPA and subscription documents for hedge clauses purporting to waive fiduciary duty except for gross negligence or fraud.
requests.format: Our counsel's markup of the exculpation, indemnification and standard-of-care sections.
requests.why: Hedge clauses narrowing fiduciary duty are an SEC exam deficiency.
requests.pass: No clause waives fiduciary duty or limits liability to gross negligence or fraud for fiduciary breaches.
requests.fail: Hedge clause retained after negotiation.

requests.request: Fund term and extension provisions, including who must approve each extension and fee treatment during extensions.
requests.why: Zombie funds keep fees running through extensions taken without required approval.
requests.pass: Extensions require LPAC or LP approval; management fee reduced or eliminated during extensions.
requests.fail: GP may extend unilaterally with full fees.

requests.request: Fee and expense definitions: list of permitted fund expenses, organizational-expense cap, and expenses borne by the manager (including operating partners).
requests.why: Funds have paid unauthorized operating-partner fees and political, charitable and entertainment expenses.
requests.pass: Closed list of permitted expenses; operating-partner costs borne by the manager or explicitly disclosed; organizational-expense cap stated.
requests.fail: Open-ended expense language; operating-partner costs charged to the fund without disclosure.

requests.request: Investment restrictions and fund-level leverage limits: concentration, geography, asset type and borrowing caps.
requests.why: Leverage and strategy outside fund documents (style drift) is an SEC exam deficiency.
requests.pass: Restrictions are specific and measurable.
requests.fail: Restrictions vague or waivable by the GP alone.
requests.verify: Fund counsel review; reconcile to holdings in confirmatory.

requests.request: GP revenue model for this fund under base and downside cases, split into management fees, transaction and monitoring fees, and carry.
requests.format: Spreadsheet with assumptions; fixed-fee share of total GP revenue in each case.
requests.why: If fixed fees pay the partners in the downside, alignment is weaker than headline carry suggests.
requests.pass: Fixed-fee share disclosed for both cases; downside case still depends meaningfully on carry. Benchmark: fixed share about 60% (2007 WP) to about two-thirds (2010 RFS).
requests.fail: Manager will not model it, or fixed fees above the Metrick-Yasuda range in the base case.
requests.verify: Rebuild from LPA terms and fund size ourselves.

requests.request: Real estate fund fee and promote terms and sponsor co-invest percentage.
requests.why: Real estate sponsors draw the same SEC fee findings as PE sponsors.
requests.pass: Fees and promote within or below the dated 2002 benchmark of 1% to 2% of committed plus a 20% promote; sponsor co-invest within 2% to 25%.
requests.fail: Fees above benchmark without justification, or sponsor co-invest below 2%.
requests.verify: Compare with current pipeline terms (benchmark is dated).

requests.request: Hedge-fund fee load and liquidity terms (management fee, performance fee, high-water mark, lock-up, gates, redemption notice).
requests.why: Pre-fee alpha of 6% to 10% is not reliably distinguishable from index put writing; the fee equating put writing to the index was about 3.6% a year.
requests.pass: All-in fee load justified against a put-writing benchmark; high-water mark present; gate and suspension terms specific.
requests.fail: All-in fees at or above about 3.6% a year for a strategy whose returns match put writing.
requests.verify: Compute put-writing replication of the manager's monthly returns.

requests.request: Fund-of-funds or SMA second-layer fee schedule and a statement of what access the second layer provides.
requests.format: Fee schedule and list of underlying managers with access constraints.
requests.why: Fund-of-funds returned less than the hedge-fund universe after the second fee layer.
requests.pass: Second-layer fees priced against demonstrable access (closed or oversubscribed managers).
requests.fail: Second layer charges full fees for access to open, available managers.

requests.request: Co-investment term sheet: price, security, and terms compared with the main fund's; any management fee, carry or monitoring fee on the co-invest vehicle.
requests.format: Side-by-side term comparison prepared by the GP.
requests.why: Co-investors have been charged fees the fund does not pay.
requests.pass: Same price, same security, same terms as the fund; any fee or carry disclosed and agreed.
requests.fail: Different security or price; undisclosed fees on the co-invest vehicle.
requests.verify: Compare with the fund's purchase agreement and capitalization table.

requests.request: GP's written explanation of why it is syndicating this deal and confirmation that the main fund is taking its full pro rata.
requests.format: Letter from the GP plus the fund's allocation calculation under its concentration limits.
requests.why: Co-invests underperform the fund deals beside them (adverse selection).
requests.pass: Syndication explained by a documented size or concentration limit; main fund takes its full pro rata.
requests.fail: Main fund not taking full pro rata; deal larger than the fund's usual size with no stated reason.
requests.verify: Verify against the fund's LPA concentration limit and its existing positions.

requests.request: Offer timeline: date the co-invest was first offered, decision deadline and list of other co-investors offered.
requests.format: Email trail and GP's syndication list.
requests.why: Offered late with a short fuse is a co-invest red flag.
requests.pass: Enough time for full company diligence; list of other offerees disclosed.
requests.fail: Short fuse that prevents independent diligence.
requests.verify: Ask other offerees for their timeline.

requests.request: Placement-agent engagement letter and fee arrangement for this fund.
requests.why: Inadequate diligence on placement agents is an SEC exam deficiency.
requests.pass: Placement fee borne by the manager or fully offset; agent registered.
requests.fail: Placement fee charged to the fund without offset.
requests.verify: Check the agent's FINRA registration on BrokerCheck.

requests.request: Deal-level track record for every realized and unrealized deal: entry and exit dates, invested, realized and unrealized value, entry and exit multiples, EBITDA at entry and exit, leverage at entry, and the deal lead.
requests.format: Spreadsheet tied to fund cash flows and audited schedules of investments.
requests.why: Track records cherry-picked, shown gross or over selective periods are an SEC exam deficiency.
requests.pass: Every deal in every vehicle listed; totals tie to fund-level cash flows and audits.
requests.fail: Deals omitted, no deal lead given, or totals that do not tie.
requests.verify: Tie deal totals to audited schedules of investments and administrator cash flows.

requests.request: Reconciliation of every marketed performance figure (IRR, TVPI, DPI, loss ratio) to fund cash flows and audited financials, gross and net, with the gross-to-net bridge by fund.
requests.format: Reconciliation workbook; gross-to-net bridge showing fees, carry and expenses.
requests.why: Gross IRR alone hides the fee drag; IRR is sensitive to holding period and financing events.
requests.pass: Our rebuild matches reported net IRR, TVPI and DPI within rounding; gross-to-net spread consistent with LPA terms.
requests.fail: Gross IRR only; rebuild differs from marketing; gross-to-net spread inconsistent with terms.
requests.verify: Rebuild from the administrator's cash-flow ledger.

requests.request: Public market equivalent analysis for every prior fund (Kaplan-Schoar PME and generalized PME), against the factor-appropriate benchmark for the strategy.
requests.format: Calculation workbook with benchmark index series and fund cash flows.
requests.why: IRR alone cannot show whether the manager beat what LPs could have earned publicly.
requests.pass: KS-PME above 1.0 against the appropriate benchmark (buyout: levered small-value index; real estate: levered public REITs; VC: public equity and GPME) for the funds that produced the record.
requests.fail: PME at or below 1.0, or PME only against the S&P 500 for a buyout strategy.
requests.verify: Compute PME ourselves from the cash flows.

requests.request: Buyout benchmark comparison: net returns against a roughly 2x-levered small, low EV/EBITDA public-stock portfolio.
requests.why: Buyout returns before fees can be largely replicated by levered small-value stocks; after about 6% a year in fees PE underperformed the replicating portfolio.
requests.pass: Net returns exceed the levered small-value replication over the funds' lives.
requests.fail: Net returns at or below the replicating portfolio.

requests.request: Put-writing benchmark comparison for any hedge, credit, merger-arbitrage, levered-carry or 'market neutral' strategy: monthly returns against a levered S&P 500 index put-writing series.
requests.format: Monthly net return series and the manager's own factor attribution.
requests.why: A strategy earning a steady spread with rare large losses is selling insurance; calm-year alpha is the premium.
requests.pass: Alpha remains after controlling for put-writing exposure.
requests.fail: Returns spanned by put writing.
requests.verify: Regress monthly returns on a put-writing index ourselves.

requests.request: Venture track record shown with and without the top one or two outcomes per fund.
requests.format: Table by fund, computed from cash flows.
requests.why: The VC aggregate is a right-tail business: dropping the best 5% of ventures makes the risk-adjusted return negative.
requests.pass: Record remains above benchmark ex top one or two outcomes, or the outlier deals were led by partners still at the firm.
requests.fail: Record collapses ex top outcome and the partner who led it has left; 'consistent singles' thesis.

requests.request: IRR and TVPI with and without the largest one or two exits for each buyout, credit or real estate fund.
requests.format: Table by fund, computed from cash flows.
requests.why: A record dominated by one exit is not evidence of repeatable skill.
requests.pass: Record remains above vintage-year median ex the top two exits.
requests.fail: Record falls below median ex the top two exits.

requests.request: Value-creation bridge for each realized deal: revenue and EBITDA growth versus leverage versus multiple change.
requests.format: Bridge per deal built from entry and exit financials.
requests.why: Prefer managers who create value through operations, not leverage, multiple expansion or momentum.
requests.pass: Operating improvement is the largest component across realized deals.
requests.fail: Returns explained mainly by leverage or multiple expansion.
requests.verify: Rebuild bridges from deal-level EBITDA and multiples.

requests.request: Deal attribution by person: who sourced and led each deal, whether they are still at the firm, and their role in this fund.
requests.format: Schedule by deal with IC memos and board seats as evidence.
requests.why: Reputation and deal access sit with partners; track records are borrowed from people who left.
requests.pass: Partners responsible for the majority of value created are still at the firm and named key persons.
requests.fail: Material share of value led by departed partners.
requests.verify: Confirm leads from IC memos, board minutes and reference calls with portfolio CEOs.

requests.request: Realized versus unrealized split and loss ratio for each fund.
requests.why: Unrealized marks in years 1 to 2 predict final results only weakly (coefficient about 0.16).
requests.pass: Conclusions on skill rest on realized results and funds older than 4 years.
requests.fail: Track record mostly unrealized, with re-up case built on year 1 to 2 marks.

requests.request: Vintage-year quartile ranking for each prior fund, with the benchmark provider named and its treatment of backfill and dead funds stated.
requests.format: Benchmark report pages and methodology statement.
requests.why: Benchmarks that exclude dead funds or include backfill overstate peers by several hundred bp; managers with recent third- or fourth-quartile funds should be declined.
requests.pass: Recent funds first or second quartile on a vintage-matched, survivor-inclusive benchmark.
requests.fail: Recent funds consistently third or fourth quartile; benchmark does not state backfill and survivorship treatment.
requests.verify: Rank the funds ourselves on a survivor-inclusive dataset.

requests.request: Monthly net returns since inception for any liquid strategy, with return distribution, drawdowns and option-like exposures.
requests.why: Sharpe, Sortino, Jensen's alpha, information ratio and M-squared can all be manufactured with derivatives or dynamic strategies.
requests.pass: We compute a manipulation-proof performance measure (MPPM) from the series; drawdowns consistent with stated strategy.
requests.fail: Only Sharpe or Sortino offered; monthly series refused.
requests.verify: Obtain the series from the administrator.

requests.request: Smoothness test: reported volatility and serial correlation of returns compared with the stated strategy's expected volatility.
requests.format: Our calculation from monthly or quarterly returns.
requests.why: Returns smooth relative to the stated strategy are the core Ponzi tell at any return level.
requests.pass: Reported volatility consistent with strategy and public comparables.
requests.fail: Returns smoother than the strategy can produce.

requests.request: Marks versus exit prices for every realization in the last 3 years (last mark before sale versus realized price).
requests.why: Valuations not following policy inflate fees and carry.
requests.pass: Exits at or above the prior mark on average.
requests.fail: Exits systematically below prior marks.
requests.verify: Tie exit prices to audited realizations.

requests.request: All quarterly letters and portfolio commentary since the predecessor fund's first close.
requests.why: Early commentary focused on refinancing, covenants or capital structure predicts worse outcomes; tone predicts about 3 to 4 points of annualized return.
requests.pass: Commentary discusses problems openly; no pattern of early refinancing and covenant language on companies later written down.
requests.fail: Problems absent from letters until write-down; capital-structure language dominating early letters.
requests.verify: Obtain the same letters from an existing LP.

requests.request: Investor-level (dollar-weighted) returns and flow history versus the fund's time-weighted return.
requests.why: Investors often buy near the top; dollar-weighted returns can be far below fund returns (internet funds: +1.5% TWR, investors lost 72%).
requests.pass: Dollar-weighted investor returns disclosed and the gap to TWR explained.
requests.fail: Large gap with flows concentrated at peaks.

requests.request: Venture mark methodology: how each round is valued, and treatment of preferences, ratchets and participation.
requests.why: Headline post-money valuations are biased upward.
requests.pass: No company marked at headline post-money where preferences, ratchets or participation exist.
requests.fail: Marks equal to headline post-money.
requests.verify: Recompute using the cap table and preference stack.

requests.request: Real estate fund returns against a levered public-REIT comparison.
requests.why: Real estate funds showed no risk-adjusted outperformance for US public pensions (1995 to 2018).
requests.pass: Net returns exceed levered public REITs over the same periods.
requests.fail: Net returns at or below levered REITs.

requests.request: CLO manager after-fee PME by vintage and management fee as % of collateral.
requests.why: CLO fees are about 50 bp of collateral and falling; underwrite after-fee PME by vintage.
requests.pass: After-fee PME above 1.0 by vintage; fees at or below about 50 bp.
requests.fail: After-fee PME below 1.0.

requests.request: Fee and expense allocation policy, covering allocation among funds, co-invest vehicles, the manager and portfolio companies.
requests.format: Written policy with approval date and LPAC review record.
requests.why: Expense misallocation favouring the adviser is a repeated SEC enforcement finding.
requests.pass: Written policy allocates shared costs pro rata and is applied consistently.
requests.fail: No policy, or policy favours the manager.
requests.verify: Test a sample of allocations against the policy.

requests.request: Three-year schedule of every portfolio-company fee (transaction, monitoring, director, operating-partner, exit, break-up) and the management-fee offset calculation.
requests.format: Schedule by company and fee type, tied to portfolio-company ledgers.
requests.why: TZP failed to offset transaction fees; fee offsets have been allocated to favour the adviser.
requests.pass: Our recomputed offset equals the offset credited to LPs; 100% offset or the LPA percentage applied.
requests.fail: Any unoffset fee or recomputation difference.
requests.verify: Obtain portfolio-company general ledgers for a sample and recompute.

requests.request: Every monitoring, advisory and services agreement between the manager or its affiliates and portfolio companies.
requests.why: Monitoring agreements with acceleration clauses on exit are a red flag.
requests.pass: No acceleration on exit; fees match the offset schedule.
requests.fail: Acceleration clauses, or fees not on the offset schedule.
requests.verify: Read each agreement; schedule fees paid on exit.

requests.request: Quarterly management-fee calculation for each prior fund after its investment period, showing the fee base and adjustments for sales, write-downs and write-offs.
requests.why: Post-commitment-period fee base not stepped down is a recurring SEC finding.
requests.pass: Fee base reduces for every disposition and write-down per the LPA.
requests.fail: Fee base unchanged after dispositions or write-downs.
requests.verify: Recompute quarter by quarter from the schedule of investments.

requests.request: Broken-deal expense schedule for 3 years and its allocation across the fund, co-investors and the manager.
requests.why: Co-investors have escaped their share of broken-deal costs at the fund's expense.
requests.pass: Broken-deal costs allocated pro rata including to co-investors.
requests.fail: Fund bears all broken-deal costs while co-investors bear none.

requests.request: Statement of who pays operating partners and consultants, with a 3-year schedule of payments by payer.
requests.format: Schedule tied to payroll and invoices.
requests.why: Unauthorized operating-partner oversight fees were charged to funds.
requests.pass: Operating-partner costs paid by the manager or disclosed and permitted by the LPA.
requests.fail: Undisclosed operating-partner fees charged to funds or companies.

requests.request: Sample of fund expenses (minimum 25 items over 3 years) with vendor invoices, including shared services such as insurance and legal.
requests.why: Funds paid all insurance premiums while the adviser negotiated a legal discount only for itself.
requests.pass: Every sampled expense permitted by the LPA and allocated per policy.
requests.fail: Impermissible expenses (political, charitable, entertainment) or skewed shared-service allocation.
requests.verify: Confirm invoices with two vendors directly.

requests.request: Fee-offset allocation across funds and co-invest vehicles for every portfolio company held by more than one vehicle.
requests.why: An adviser allocated offsets among funds in a way that favoured itself ($2.3M fine plus $10.4M reimbursement).
requests.pass: Offsets allocated pro rata to ownership in every vehicle.
requests.fail: Offsets concentrated in vehicles with lower fee rates.

requests.request: Related-party property management, construction, leasing or financing fees charged to real estate fund assets, with LPAC consents.
requests.format: Fee schedule and LPAC consent records.
requests.why: Related-party fees without LPAC consent are a recurring SEC finding for real estate sponsors.
requests.pass: Every related-party fee consented by the LPAC and at market rates.
requests.fail: Related-party fees without consent.

requests.request: Valuation policy, including methodology by asset type, frequency, governance and escalation.
requests.format: Board- or committee-approved policy with version history.
requests.why: Valuations not following stated policy inflate fees and carry.
requests.pass: Policy specific by asset type; independent party values Level 3 assets.
requests.fail: Policy gives the manager full discretion.
requests.verify: Test a sample of marks against the policy.

requests.request: Valuation-committee minutes for 3 years.
requests.why: Infinity Q fabricated valuation-committee minutes; real minutes show dissent.
requests.pass: Minutes show independent members and recorded challenge or dissent.
requests.fail: No dissent ever recorded; minutes appear templated.

requests.request: Engagement letters and reports of every third-party valuation firm named in marketing or fund documents.
requests.format: Signed engagement letters and full reports for the last 3 years.
requests.why: SQN's principal prepared the valuations himself while telling investors an independent expert did.
requests.pass: Engagement letter exists and scope covers the stated positions; the firm confirms on a call that it performed the work.
requests.fail: No engagement letter, or the firm does not confirm.
requests.verify: Call the valuation firm at an independently sourced number.

requests.request: List of persons with write access to pricing inputs and models, including pricing-service inputs, with system access logs.
requests.format: Access-rights report from the pricing system.
requests.why: Infinity Q's CIO altered inputs to the 'independent' Bloomberg BVAL models; third-party pricing is not independence.
requests.pass: No investment professional can alter pricing inputs; changes logged and reviewed.
requests.fail: Portfolio manager or CIO can alter inputs.
requests.verify: Confirm access rights with the administrator.

requests.request: Administrator's independent price for a sample of Level 3 positions (at least 10 positions or 25% of Level 3 NAV).
requests.why: Pricing process disagrees with the administrator's in 3.6% of managers.
requests.pass: Administrator price within 5% of manager mark for every sampled position, or differences explained.
requests.fail: Material unexplained differences.
requests.verify: Receive the report directly from the administrator.

requests.request: Sample of current marks compared with the written valuation policy, with fees and carry recomputed on any corrected NAV.
requests.why: Marks outside policy inflate fees and carry.
requests.pass: All sampled marks comply with policy; no fee impact.
requests.fail: Marks outside policy that changed fees or carry.

requests.request: LPAC minutes and consents for 3 years.
requests.why: LPAC consent skipped for conflicted transactions is a recurring SEC finding.
requests.pass: Every affiliated transaction has a matching LPAC consent before the transaction.
requests.fail: Missing or after-the-fact consents.
requests.verify: Ask an LPAC member to confirm.

requests.request: List of every affiliated or related-party transaction from the audited financial statements over 3 years, cross-referenced to its LPAC consent.
requests.why: Undisclosed conflicts.
requests.pass: Every audit-footnote related-party item has a consent.
requests.fail: Any related-party item without consent.

requests.request: Allocation policy and the log of every cross-trade and investment allocation among funds, accounts and co-investors for 3 years.
requests.why: Undisclosed conflicts in allocations and cross-trades are the first SEC deficiency.
requests.pass: Allocations follow the policy and every cross-trade has LPAC approval.
requests.fail: Allocations deviate from policy or cross-trades lack approval.

requests.request: Co-invest allocation policy and the list of co-invests offered in the last fund: to whom, on what terms, and whether the fund took its full pro rata.
requests.why: Co-invest adverse selection and favouritism.
requests.pass: Allocations follow policy; fund took full pro rata in every co-invest.
requests.fail: Fund took less than pro rata; co-invests offered selectively without policy basis.

requests.request: Term-extension history for every prior fund with the approval obtained for each.
requests.why: Zombie funds extended without approval keep fees running.
requests.pass: Every extension approved per the LPA; fees reduced as required.
requests.fail: Extensions without approval.
requests.verify: Match to LPA requirements and LPAC minutes.

requests.request: Reconciliation of current holdings and fund-level debt to the LPA's strategy, concentration and leverage limits (and to 13F filings where filed).
requests.format: Holdings report from the administrator and 13F filings.
requests.why: Style drift: strategy not matching the stated mandate.
requests.pass: All holdings and leverage within limits.
requests.fail: Breaches or holdings outside mandate.
requests.verify: Use administrator holdings and public 13F data.

requests.request: List of every departure of a named key person or senior partner across all funds, with the date LPs were told and any key-person vote.
requests.format: Schedule plus notices sent to LPs.
requests.why: Key-person events not followed or disclosed is an SEC deficiency.
requests.pass: Every key-person event noticed to LPs promptly and handled per LPA.
requests.fail: Undisclosed or late-disclosed key-person events.

requests.request: Compliance manual and code of ethics.
requests.format: Current versions with annual review evidence.
requests.why: Baseline for conflicts, personal trading and valuation governance.
requests.pass: Current, reviewed annually, with a named CCO who is not an investment professional.
requests.fail: Outdated manual; CCO is also CFO or CIO without mitigation.

requests.request: Manager's own diligence files on service providers, placement agents and alternative data vendors.
requests.why: Inadequate diligence on service providers is an SEC deficiency.
requests.pass: Documented diligence for each material vendor.
requests.fail: No files.

requests.request: Statement of the manager's investor AML program: whether one is voluntarily run, which administrator performs investor KYC, and whether the administrator files SARs.
requests.format: AML policy and administrator's KYC service description.
requests.why: The Investment Adviser AML rule is delayed to Jan. 1, 2028; until then adviser AML is contractual and voluntary.
requests.pass: Voluntary AML program or administrator-performed investor KYC with SAR filing.
requests.fail: No program and no administrator KYC.
requests.verify: Confirm KYC scope with the administrator.

requests.request: Ownership chart of the GP and management company down to individuals, with co-investor ownership where relevant.
requests.format: Chart with percentages, certified by counsel.
requests.why: No federal BOI registry exists for domestic companies; collect and verify ownership directly.
requests.pass: Chart complete to natural persons; matches ADV Schedule A/B.
requests.fail: Undisclosed owners or mismatch with ADV.

requests.request: Disclosure of sponsor-level secondary-liability exposures in the portfolio: False Claims Act, ERISA multiemployer withdrawal liability, control-person, FCPA.
requests.why: Sponsor liability can reach funds (Riordan Lewis & Haden FCA settlement; Sun Capital ERISA; Och-Ziff FCPA).
requests.pass: Exposures identified with mitigation.
requests.fail: Unassessed exposure in healthcare or government-contract companies.

requests.request: Carry and GP-ownership allocation by person for the current and prior fund, with vesting schedules.
requests.format: Schedule by person and fund, certified by the CFO.
requests.why: Underprovision of carry to non-founders predicts senior departures (stayers held 16% carry and 23% ownership vs 9% and 13% for leavers).
requests.pass: People who generated the track record hold meaningful carry; founders holding most carry will be in seat for the fund's life.
requests.fail: Founders hold most carry while deal leads hold little, or founders will not be in seat.
requests.verify: Compare change from prior fund; interview two non-founder partners.

requests.request: Formal succession plan: who makes investment decisions, who owns LP relationships, and what happens economically if a founder steps back.
requests.why: Fewer than half of GPs have a formal plan; 96% of LPs say succession readiness is decisive for re-ups.
requests.pass: Written plan names successors who have led at scale and states how carry and ownership transfer.
requests.fail: No formal plan in a founder-led firm.

requests.request: Team compensation and retention arrangements: salary bands, bonus pools and deferred compensation.
requests.why: Alignment and retention.
requests.pass: Retention tools cover the deal team beyond the founders.
requests.fail: No retention tools below founders.

requests.request: Senior-hire record: senior investment and operating professionals added since the funds that earned the track record.
requests.why: Deal pace doubling without the operating bench doubling is associated with worse outcomes.
requests.pass: Senior bench grew in proportion to fund size and deal pace.
requests.fail: Fund size or deal pace doubled without matching senior hires.
requests.verify: Verify against ADV and org charts over time.

requests.request: Administrator agreement and description of the NAV process, showing the administrator computes NAV from its own records (bank, custodian and broker feeds).
requests.why: No independent NAV was the Madoff structure.
requests.pass: Administrator independently sources positions and cash and computes NAV.
requests.fail: Administrator relies on manager-supplied records, or self-administration.
requests.verify: Confirm on the unsolicited administrator call.

requests.request: Custody agreements and the most recent custodian statements for every account.
requests.why: Assets that cannot be verified with a third party (about 19% of managers).
requests.pass: Custodian is independent and statements match administrator holdings.
requests.fail: Affiliated custodian or holdings mismatch.

requests.request: Prime brokerage and derivatives agreements with every counterparty, and exposure reports from each.
requests.why: Archegos built concentrated exposure across prime brokers, none of whom saw the whole book.
requests.pass: Aggregate exposure across all counterparties consistent with mandate.
requests.fail: Exposure visible only counterparty by counterparty.
requests.verify: Confirm balances with each prime broker.

requests.request: Audited financial statements of every fund for at least 3 years.
requests.why: Unaudited fund is an automatic pass; late or qualified statements are red flags.
requests.pass: Unqualified opinions, delivered on time, by an auditor sized for the mandate.
requests.fail: Qualified opinion, late statements, unaudited vehicle.

requests.request: Auditor engagement letters and management letters for 3 years.
requests.why: Management letters reveal control weaknesses not in the opinion.
requests.pass: No unremediated significant deficiencies.
requests.fail: Repeat control findings.

requests.request: Auditor history for all vehicles: every auditor change with the reason, and the auditor's size relative to the mandate.
requests.format: Schedule plus resignation or dismissal correspondence.
requests.why: Non-Big 4 auditor combined with internal pricing is associated with misrepresentation; Madoff used a two-partner auditor.
requests.pass: Auditor sized for the mandate; no unexplained change.
requests.fail: Unexplained change; small auditor plus internal pricing.

requests.request: Bank signatory list and wire-approval matrix for every fund account, issued by the bank or administrator.
requests.format: Bank- or administrator-issued document, not manager-prepared.
requests.why: In 16% of managers the wire-signature process disagrees with the administrator's.
requests.pass: Bank/administrator matrix matches the manager's description; dual authorization with at least one independent party.
requests.fail: Any mismatch, or matrix only from the manager.
requests.verify: Obtain directly from the bank or administrator.

requests.request: Reconciliation of every distribution in the last 3 years to its source account and to underlying portfolio cash flow.
requests.format: Distribution ledger tied to bank statements and portfolio-company or asset cash flows.
requests.why: GPB paid 'operating cash flow' distributions from new investor capital.
requests.pass: Every distribution traced to realizations or portfolio income.
requests.fail: Distributions funded by new capital or borrowing without disclosure; fixed distribution rate on an illiquid fund.
requests.verify: Trace a sample through bank statements obtained from the bank.

requests.request: List of major data and pricing vendors with any changes in the last 3 years and reasons.
requests.why: 11% of managers switched a major data vendor in the last 3 years.
requests.pass: Changes explained.
requests.fail: Unexplained switches around valuation dates.

requests.request: Cybersecurity, business-continuity and IT policies, with latest penetration test and BCP test results.
requests.why: Operational resilience of the manager.
requests.pass: Annual tests performed; critical findings remediated.
requests.fail: No testing.
requests.verify: Interview the CTO or outsourced provider.

requests.request: Written confirmation of every number given in management meetings (AUM, performance, team size, pipeline) with the document each ties to.
requests.format: Schedule prepared by us from meeting notes, confirmed by the manager.
requests.why: In 20% of managers verbal figures contradicted their own documents.
requests.pass: Every verbal figure ties to a document.
requests.fail: Any gap; treat as a finding.
requests.verify: Tie each to the data room.

requests.request: Subscription-line and NAV-facility agreements, borrowing history and LPAC consents for every prior fund.
requests.why: Facility usage inflates IRR and DPI.
requests.pass: Usage within LPA caps; consents obtained.
requests.fail: Usage beyond caps or without consent.

requests.request: Quarterly sub-line disclosures for each prior fund: facility size, balance, days outstanding and uncalled-capital estimate.
requests.why: Sub lines above reference points distort returns.
requests.pass: Within 15% to 25% of commitments and 180 days outstanding, or disclosed.
requests.fail: Above 25% or beyond 180 days without disclosure.

requests.request: Synthetic DPI and IRR for each prior fund excluding NAV-loan-funded distributions, with recallability terms.
requests.why: Carry paid on NAV-loan-funded distributions and IRR/DPI inflated near a fundraise.
requests.pass: Synthetic figures produced; no carry on borrowed distributions.
requests.fail: Refusal; carry paid on borrowed distributions.

requests.request: History of every GP-led secondary and continuation vehicle sponsored by the manager, with LPAC approvals, fairness opinions and election results.
requests.why: GP sits on both sides of a GP-led.
requests.pass: Each had LPAC consent, status quo option and an independent fairness opinion.
requests.fail: Missing process protections.

requests.request: For any insurer-affiliated manager: affiliated insurer's statutory statements, Schedule S, and consolidated risk-based capital including affiliated captives.
requests.why: Manager lends policyholders' money into its own deals; affiliated reinsurance cut average RBC by about 53 points when adjusted.
requests.pass: RBC adequate after consolidating captives.
requests.fail: RBC adequacy depends on affiliated captives.
requests.verify: Pull filings from the state insurance regulator.

requests.request: For any insurer-affiliated manager: affiliated-transaction policy and independent valuation of affiliated private placements.
requests.why: Life-insurer private-placement lending reached about $849B (14% of balance sheets) in 2024, driven by PE-owned insurers.
requests.pass: Independent valuation of affiliated placements; policy requires independent approval.
requests.fail: Affiliated placements valued by the manager.

requests.request: Full company diligence package for the co-investment: QoE, legal diligence, debt documents and CEO assessment (not the GP's IC memo).
requests.format: Third-party reports addressed to or relied on by us.
requests.why: Co-investors must underwrite the company on a compressed timetable; the GP's memo is advocacy.
requests.pass: All reports received with reliance; issues resolved.
requests.fail: Only the IC memo offered.
requests.verify: Run the Chapter 5 private-equity request set.

requests.request: Co-investment information and exit rights: tag-along, drag-along, information parity with the fund, transfer rights.
requests.format: Co-invest vehicle LPA or shareholders' agreement.
requests.why: Co-investors without information parity or exit rights are trapped.
requests.pass: Tag and drag on same terms as the fund; information parity; transfer permitted.
requests.fail: No information parity or tag rights.

requests.request: Sponsor's uncalled capital and reserve policy in the fund that owns the company.
requests.format: Fund's latest capital account summary and reserve policy.
requests.why: Sponsor dry powder supported PE-backed companies in 2008-09.
requests.pass: Fund has reserves sufficient for a follow-on in the downside case.
requests.fail: Fund fully called with no reserves.
requests.verify: Confirm uncalled capital with the administrator.

requests.request: Downside case for the co-investment that assumes at least one CEO change and an extended hold.
requests.why: 69% of buyouts change CEO; holds averaged 5.5 years with no change and 8.5 with two.
requests.pass: Downside case still returns capital at an 8.5-year hold.
requests.fail: Model assumes a short hold and no CEO change only.

requests.request: Aggregate exposure of the lead sponsor or family office to the company across all counterparties and vehicles.
requests.why: Archegos concentrated exposure across counterparties.
requests.pass: Total exposure disclosed and within stated limits.
requests.fail: Exposure not disclosed.

requests.request: Disclosure of any lender to the company affiliated with the equity sponsor, and how credit-agreement amendments are approved.
requests.format: Lender list and credit agreement amendment provisions.
requests.why: Same-sponsor credit creates conflicts in amendments.
requests.pass: Affiliated lending disclosed; amendments require unaffiliated lender approval.
requests.fail: Undisclosed affiliated lender controlling amendments.

requests.request: Comparison of the co-invest deal size with the fund's usual deal size and with the sponsor's recent deal pace.
requests.why: Larger-than-usual deals and doubling deal pace are co-invest red flags.
requests.pass: Deal within the fund's usual size range.
requests.fail: Deal materially larger than usual.
requests.verify: Compare with fund schedule of investments.

requests.request: Investment policy statement, policy portfolio, spending rule and liquidity policy of the allocator, fund-of-funds or OCIO.
requests.why: Spending and liquidity rules set how much illiquidity the program can carry (Yale: about 5.25% spending with 80% weight on prior year).
requests.pass: Policy documents current; spending or payout smoothing documented.
requests.fail: No written policy or liquidity rule.

requests.request: Commitment pacing model with the last five years of forecast versus actual calls and distributions.
requests.why: Pacing by calendar rather than manager quality; liquidity shortfalls when distributions stop.
requests.pass: Forecast errors explained; pacing follows manager quality first.
requests.fail: No model, or large unexplained variances.
requests.verify: Tie actuals to capital account statements.

requests.request: Manager roster with commitment, NAV, fees paid as % of actively managed assets (not total assets), and each manager's net performance against a passive alternative.
requests.format: Roster schedule tied to capital account statements.
requests.why: Connecticut reported fees on total assets and lagged a plain 60/40 by over 1 point a year.
requests.pass: Fees reported on active assets; most managers beat their passive alternative net.
requests.fail: Fees on total assets only; managers lagging passive retained.

requests.request: Delegation of authority: who hires and terminates managers, how fast, and whether the decision-maker is paid on assets retained.
requests.why: Governance is a return driver (PRINCO staff fully empowered on execution).
requests.pass: Staff can terminate managers promptly; pay not tied to assets retained.
requests.fail: Termination requires slow board process; pay based on assets retained.

requests.request: CIO and investment-staff tenure history.
requests.format: Schedule of CIOs and senior staff with dates.
requests.why: Connecticut cycled through 8 CIOs and 4 interim CIOs.
requests.pass: Stable CIO tenure; turnover explained.
requests.fail: Frequent CIO turnover.

requests.request: Concentration list: managers where the allocator is the anchor, sole or dominant client.
requests.format: Schedule with share of each manager's AUM.
requests.why: Connecticut paid high fees where it was a manager's sole or dominant client.
requests.pass: Anchor positions justified with fee concessions.
requests.fail: Sole-client relationships at full fees.
requests.verify: Check manager ADVs for client counts.

requests.request: Unfunded commitments by vintage and the liquidity sources that cover them (cash, distributions, credit lines, secondaries).
requests.format: Schedule tied to capital account statements.
requests.why: Liquidity can vanish across assets at once; distributions stop while calls continue.
requests.pass: Unfunded commitments covered without relying on distributions or secondary sales.
requests.fail: Coverage depends on distributions continuing.
requests.verify: Tie to statements and credit agreements.

requests.request: Liquidity stress test: two years of zero distributions with calls continuing, funded without forced sales, and the price assumed for any secondary sale.
requests.why: LP portfolios traded at about 87% of NAV in H1 2026; tail-end at 25%+ discounts.
requests.pass: Program meets calls for two years with no distributions; any secondary sale priced at or below 87% of NAV (68% for real estate).
requests.fail: Plan relies on secondary sales at par.

requests.request: Re-up record: managers re-upped versus dropped in the last five years and the subsequent performance of both groups.
requests.why: Endowments' PE edge came mainly from better re-up decisions; bank-selected funds lagged.
requests.pass: Dropped managers' successor funds underperformed re-upped ones.
requests.fail: No re-up discipline evident.

requests.request: Roster size against investment staff: number of managers and commitments per staff member.
requests.why: Over-diversified rosters dilute attention without adding safety ('fewer, better, stronger').
requests.pass: Roster count stable or falling relative to staff.
requests.fail: Roster growing faster than staff; many small commitments.

requests.request: For thematic vehicles (AI, crypto, space, climate and similar): entry valuation against the sector's history and the date the theme peaked in media and fund-launch counts.
requests.format: Sponsor's valuation comparison and launch-count data.
requests.why: Thematic launches buy at the top: specialized ETFs lose about 30% risk-adjusted over five years.
requests.pass: Entry valuation at or below sector history; launch not after the media peak.
requests.fail: Launch after a media peak at a premium valuation.

requests.request: Unsolicited direct confirmation from the fund administrator of NAV, holdings, investor capital balances, the wire-approval matrix and the list of vehicles serviced.
requests.format: Call notes and written confirmation from the administrator on its letterhead.
requests.why: THE ONE CHECK: catches Madoff, Infinity Q, SQN and the 16% of managers whose wire-approval story differs.
requests.pass: Administrator confirms every item without manager intermediation.
requests.fail: Administrator cannot confirm, defers to the manager, or contradicts the manager.
requests.verify: Use an independently sourced phone number; do not pre-notify the manager of timing.

requests.request: Unsolicited direct confirmation from the auditor of engagement, scope, opinion type and any auditor resignation history.
requests.format: Call notes; written confirmation where the auditor permits.
requests.why: Auditor too small, changed or unaware of vehicles.
requests.pass: Auditor confirms engagement for every vehicle and unqualified opinions.
requests.fail: Auditor unaware of a vehicle or reports scope limitation.

requests.request: Unsolicited direct confirmation from the custodian and each prime broker of assets held and balances.
requests.why: Assets that do not exist (Madoff) or exposure split across brokers (Archegos).
requests.pass: Holdings match administrator records.
requests.fail: Mismatch or refusal.

requests.request: Unsolicited direct confirmation from each named valuation firm of its engagement, scope and the positions it valued.
requests.format: Call notes and the firm's confirmation.
requests.why: SQN's 'independent' valuations were prepared by the principal.
requests.pass: Firm confirms engagement and scope.
requests.fail: Firm denies or narrows the engagement.

requests.request: Independent operational due diligence report on the manager.
requests.format: Report from a third-party ODD provider engaged by us, scored against the Trust and Delegation base rates.
requests.why: Run ODD to the same standard on a hot manager; ODD team holds a veto.
requests.pass: No high-severity findings; scorecard better than base rates.
requests.fail: Any high-severity finding unresolved.
requests.verify: Provider engaged and paid by us.

requests.request: Site visit to the manager's operating office, including walkthrough of trade, cash and valuation processes.
requests.why: Refusal of an on-site visit is a red flag.
requests.pass: Visit completed; processes observed match descriptions.
requests.fail: Visit refused or deferred.

requests.request: LP-side fund counsel review memo of the LPA, side letter and MFN.
requests.format: Memo by our counsel against ILPA Principles 3.0 and the 10.15 contract list.
requests.why: Everything needed must be in the LPA or side letter.
requests.pass: All 10.15 protections obtained or exceptions approved.
requests.fail: Material protections missing.

requests.request: Diligence on the placement agent: registration, disciplinary history, fee and conflicts.
requests.why: SEC exam deficiency 11.
requests.pass: Registered with no disciplinary history.
requests.fail: Unregistered or disciplined agent.

requests.request: Benchmark data provider's statement of what its dataset excludes (backfill, dead funds, leverage adjustment).
requests.why: Database bias: backfill 500+ bp a year; survivorship 379 bp to 4.4%.
requests.pass: Data vintage-matched, survivor-inclusive and backfill-free.
requests.fail: Undisclosed treatment.

requests.request: Reference calls with at least three existing LPs (including one that did not re-up) and two former senior employees.
requests.why: Endowments outperformed by deciding better whether to re-up; leavers know team issues.
requests.pass: References consistent with data room.
requests.fail: References contradict data room.
requests.verify: Source at least one reference independently of the manager.

requests.request: Independent QoE, legal and CEO assessment reports on the co-investment target.
requests.format: Reports by our or reliance-granting providers.
requests.why: Do not rely on the GP's IC memo.
requests.pass: Reports received with reliance.
requests.fail: No reliance.

requests.request: Executed side letter with MFN covering the best fee tier and all negotiated protections.
requests.why: Fee-tier spreads of about 91 bp; MFN that excludes the best tier.
requests.pass: Side letter executed with MFN to best tier and all negotiated items.
requests.fail: MFN carve-outs for best tier.

requests.request: Final LPA and subscription documents conformed to negotiated terms, with a redline against the reviewed draft.
requests.why: Late changes to negotiated terms.
requests.pass: Redline shows only agreed changes.
requests.fail: Unagreed changes.

requests.request: Capital-call wire instructions confirmed by call-back to the administrator.
requests.format: Administrator-issued instructions confirmed by phone at an independently sourced number.
requests.why: Wire diversion and instructions that do not match the administrator's records.
requests.pass: Instructions match the administrator's records and the fund's bank account.
requests.fail: Instructions differ or come only from the manager.

requests.request: Bring-down certificate: no material changes since the DDQ in personnel, litigation, regulatory matters, service providers or performance.
requests.why: Changes between diligence and closing.
requests.pass: Clean certificate.
requests.fail: Disclosed adverse change.
requests.verify: Refresh the background and ADV checks.

requests.request: Confirmation of LPAC seat or observer right where negotiated.
requests.why: LPAC consents protect against conflicted transactions.
requests.pass: Seat confirmed.
requests.fail: Not confirmed.

requests.request: Executed co-invest vehicle documents confirming same price, security and terms as the fund, and fee and carry as agreed.
requests.why: Co-invests charged fees the fund does not pay.
requests.pass: Terms as agreed.
requests.fail: Deviations.

requests.request: Quarterly ILPA Reporting Template, including fees, expenses, offsets and facility usage.
requests.format: ILPA template within the LPA deadline each quarter.
requests.why: No federal rule requires quarterly statements.
requests.pass: Delivered on time; fees and offsets reconcile to prior quarter and to audit.
requests.fail: Late or non-ILPA reports.

requests.request: Annual ILPA Performance Template with gross and net IRR and TVPI with and without the subscription facility.
requests.why: Sub-line-inflated IRR.
requests.pass: Delivered annually; without-facility figures shown.
requests.fail: Not delivered.

requests.request: Quarterly capital account statement, issued or tied out by the administrator.
requests.why: Statements from the manager only were the Madoff pattern.
requests.pass: Statement issued by the administrator and reconciles to our records.
requests.fail: Manager-issued only, or breaks.

requests.request: Annual audited financial statements of the fund by the named auditor, delivered by the LPA deadline.
requests.why: Unaudited or late audits.
requests.pass: Unqualified opinion by the named auditor, on time.
requests.fail: Late, qualified or auditor changed without notice.

requests.request: Capital-call notices stating purpose, investment, and any subscription-line repayment.
requests.why: Sub-line use hides call timing.
requests.pass: Purpose stated; sub-line repayment shown.
requests.fail: Generic notices.

requests.request: Distribution notices identifying source (realization, income, NAV-loan proceeds, recallable amounts).
requests.why: NAV-funded and recallable distributions; distributions funded by new capital (GPB).
requests.pass: Source stated for every distribution.
requests.fail: Source not stated.

requests.request: Quarterly subscription-line and NAV-facility disclosure: size, balance, days outstanding, uncalled-capital estimate and use of proceeds.
requests.why: Facility usage beyond reference points.
requests.pass: Within 15% to 25% of commitments and 180 days, or disclosed.
requests.fail: Undisclosed usage.
